We extend this technique to the THz range, describing the design and performance of a THz diffuse reflectance system.

articleTitle: Application of a "grid" volume resonator to the radiation generation in THz range
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: In present paper it is shown that nonrelativistic and low-relativistic electron beams passing through such structures can generate in terahertz range. Analysis of grid resonator parameters is done. Merits and demerits of such a system are discussed.

articleTitle: Compression of frequency-swept microwave pulses using a helically corrugated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Microwave pulse compression is an important area of research in vacuum electronics, with important applications for linear accelerators, RADAR and non-linear testing. The principles and methods of pulse compression differ greatly depending on the application. The concept of producing ultra-high-power nanosecond microwave pulses, using passive sweep-frequency compression, was studied. A novel waveguide with a helical corrugation of its inner surface was used as the microwave pulse compressor. This structure couples a TE/sub 11/ traveling wave with a near cut-off TE/sub 21/ wave producing a region far from cut-off with a large change in group velocity with frequency. A 2.08 meter long copper helical waveguide was used to compress a 67 ns, 5.7 kW frequency-swept pulse from a high power TWT, driven by a swept solid-state source, to a 2.8 ns 68 kW pulse containing /spl sim/50% of the energy of the input pulse. The dispersion characteristics of the helically corrugated waveguide were investigated both experimentally and theoretically. A vector network analyser was used to measure experimentally the dispersion characteristics of complex waveguides and the code MAGIC was used to calculate the dispersion theoretically. Good agreement between experimental results and theoretical predictions was observed.

articleTitle: Computer simulations of gyrotrons with coaxial cavities
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Computer simulations of high power coaxial gyrotrons have been done by using modified code MAGY. 1.5 MW, 165 GHz FZK (Germany) and industrial 2 MW/CW, 170 GHz CRPP/EPFL, FZK, TEKES and males Electron Devices gyrotrons have been used as basic configurations for modelling. Results of simulations, their comparison with experiments and discussion on advantages and limitations of gyrotron computer simulations will be presented.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave measurements of nuclear waste glass melts
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: 137 GHz heterodyne receiver measurements with hollow ceramic HE/sub 11/ waveguides are being applied to nuclear waste glass melt monitoring of temperature, emissivity, and surface fluctuations/flow in both laboratory and engineering scale melters at temperatures as high as 1500/spl deg/C. New insights are being provided on molten glass/salt interaction and glass pour dynamics.

articleTitle: Characterization of a quantum cascade laser as local oscillator in a heterodyne receiver at 2.5 THz
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A quantum cascade laser operating at 2.5 THz has been investigated with respect to performance parameters which are relevant for a local oscillator in a heterodyne receiver. The beam profile has been measured and transformed in to a close to Gaussian profile resulting in a good matching between the field patterns of the quantum cascade laser and the antenna of a superconducting hot electron bolometric mixer. Noise temperature measurements with the hot electron bolometer and a 2.5 THz quantum cascade laser yielded the same result as with a gas laser as local oscillator.

articleTitle: High-power millimeter wave harmonic generator
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: It is shown from theory and computations that a uniform rectangular dielectric-lined waveguide is an attractive structure that can be part of an efficient generator of harmonic radiation. When a bunched beam is injected into this structure, intense radiation at a harmonic of the bunch injection frequency can be generated, provided the phase velocity of the design mode of structure at the desired harmonic is synchronous with the beam velocity. An example is presented for efficient generation of multi-MW power at 103 GHz, using a 34.3 GHz drive beam.

articleTitle: THz evanescent field spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The attenuated total internal reflection spectroscopy at terahertz frequencies is considered. We have focused on the information carried by the interaction of the evanescent field with the optical material in the place of an optical tunneling barrier.

articleTitle: Beam optics analysis
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Beam optics analysis is currently being used to design multiple beam and sheet beam electron guns and collectors. The advanced graphical user interface and adaptive meshing provide a powerful, user-friendly design tool for simulating complex geometries. Characteristics of the design code are predicted as well as integration of computer optimization routines.

articleTitle: Effects of carrier degeneracy and conduction band nonparabolicity on the simulation of HgCdTe photovoltaic devices
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: By using the analytic model of the MCT device simulation, R/sub d/-V curve comparisons are made with the carrier density approximations by considering (1) both carrier degeneracy and conduction band nonparabolicity, (2) only carrier degeneracy, and (3) only conduction band nonparabolicity. The effects of the omission of carrier degeneracy and conduction band nonparabolicity on each of the four types of dark current mechanisms are evaluated, which is found to lead to an enormous deviation in the simulation of MCT devices, especially for LWIR devices with heavy doping.

articleTitle: Terahertz transmission of subwavelength planar fractals
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Optical transmission properties of subwavelength planar fractals in terahertz (THz) frequency region are studied by means of time-domain spectroscopy. The transmission spectra with multiple pass bands and stop bands are observed. The tunable photonic band gaps are realized by changing the angle between the principle axis of planar fractal and the polarization of THz wave. The possible application of the subwavelength optical component is discussed. We attribute the detected transmittance from subwavelength fractals to localized resonance.

articleTitle: Application of THz imaging for biological tissues
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: An in vitro biological tissue sample is measured using a THz 2D-EO imaging system. The structure of the sample is successfully identified in the spectroscopic image as low transmittance lines. These lines are caused by the difference of water content in the tissues or by Fabry-Perot effect at the interfaces between different tissues.

articleTitle: Real-time two-dimensional terahertz tomography
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Real-time two-dimensional (2D) terahertz (THz) tomography is proposed for 2D cross-sectional imaging of moving objects. The proposed method is based on combined use of noncollinear two-dimensional free-space electro-optics sampling (2D-FSEOS) and line focusing of terahertz beam. There are no needs of mechanical scanning elements for time delay and sample position, which are essential for conventional THz tomography. We apply real-time 2D THz tomography to monitoring of the paint thickness in a moving paint sample. The proposed method provides a powerful tool for noninvasive and noncontact probing in the fields of nondestructive testing and biomedical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Development of a THz gyrotron using a pulse magnet
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: An ultra-high frequency gyrotron is being developed by using a pulse magnet. We have achieved the highest field intensity of 20.2 T. High frequency operation at the second harmonic will achieve 1.01 THz. Corresponding cavity mode is TE/sub 6,11,1/. The results of the first trial for a THz gyrotron are presented.

articleTitle: New schemes of gyro-devices with frequency multiplication
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Methods of significant improvement of electron bunching at high cyclotron harmonics in cyclotron resonance masers (CRMs) are proposed for weakly relativistic electron energy. A possibility to achieve efficient millimeter radiation from thus prebunched beams is demonstrated. Proposed schemes can be rated as steps to creating powerful selective devices operating in THz frequency range.

articleTitle: Microwave plasma catalyst
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The emissions from transport vehicles have dramatically increased over the last 30 years and huge sums of money are being invested in the reduction of vehicle pollution. The current method for treating these gases is using a catalytic converter, which has a honeycomb of porous ceramic. Once the catalyst has been heated to over 300 /spl deg/C the unwanted molecules are ripped from their compounds and stick to the catalyst where they bind with other similar atoms and are then released into the atmosphere. In addition, the internal combustion engine does not burn with 100% efficiency, some of the, nonburnt fuel causes the release of hydrocarbons (HC) and due to inadequate mixing with the air molecules exit the engine as carbon monoxide (CO). Additionally the combustion combines nitrogen with oxygen to form oxides of nitrogen (NOx). This paper presents the microwave plasma catalyst and its effective use against vehicles against gases and particulates.

articleTitle: Infrared absorption spectrum of magnesium double donors in silicon
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: It is well known that magnesium behaves likes an interstitial double donor in silicon and the ionization energies at liquid helium temperature are 107.50 and 256.47 meV for neutral and singly ionized magnesium donors, respectively. Recently, we have found several spectral lines unobserved before from the high-resolution infrared absorption spectra of magnesium-doped silicon measured at liquid helium temperature demonstrating the existence of other neutral and singly ionized magnesium donors in silicon. Compared with the well known donors mentioned previously, they are shallower donors with smaller ionization energies. Our study clearly indicates that there are multiple neutral and singly ionized magnesium donors in silicon. We have also observed some unusual spectra surprisingly inconsistent with typical donor spectra in silicon.

articleTitle: Suppression of the velocity-spread influence on a coaxial-waveguide cyclotron autoresonance maser
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The influence of the electron-beam velocity spread on the coaxial-waveguide cyclotron autoresonance maser (CARM) is investigated by nonlinear simulation. It is found that the velocity spread substantially decreases the power indeed, but it may be suppressed efficiently by a tapered magnetic field.

articleTitle: Noninvasive detection of concealed powders using terahertz wave scattering
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We propose a THz-wave device for the nondestructive detection of illicit drugs and hazardous substances hidden in sealed envelopes. A fast process of selecting suspicious envelopes is realized by monitoring the THz waves scattered from the target. Experimental results on this powder detection technique are presented.

articleTitle: Terahertz therapy - a new method of treatment of cardiovascular pathology
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: First, electromagnetic radiation of terahertz range at molecular spectrum frequencies of nitride oxide (from 150.176 to 150.664 GHz) is used in clinical practice for 30 patients with stenocardia and arterial hypertension. Antianginal, hypotensive, and hypocoagulative action of terahertz therapy is exposed.

articleTitle: Design and cold-testing of a high gain, Ku-band gyroklystron
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: At the University of Maryland, we have been evaluating the use of gyroklystrons to drive RF accelerators. In order to use our 500 kV, 500 A system to energize a 17 GHz accelerator structure built by the Haimson Research Corporation, we need a large-signal gain of nearly 50 dB. To accomplish this goal, we have designed a six-cavity circuit in which the first three cavities operate near the cyclotron frequency and the last three cavities operate near the second harmonic. Adequate efficiencies and gains are predicted via numerical simulations with the MAGYKL code, even for average perpendicular to parallel velocity ratios (alphas) as low as one.

articleTitle: Optical control in active terahertz waveguides
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We demonstrate an optical control of waveguides for THz QCLs. THz QCLs can be modulated by optically induced carrier plasma at the laser facet and pulses of < 100 fs length. In addition, we show an interaction of few cycle THz pulses with quantum cascade heterostructures.

articleTitle: Laboratory simulation at microwave frequencies of auroral kilometric radiation emission mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: When a beam of electrons encounters an increasing magnetic field along its vector of motion, conservation of the magnetic moment results in the formation of a crescent or horseshoe shaped velocity distribution. A scenario analogous to this occurs in the terrestrial auroral zone where particles are accelerated into the polar regions of the Earth's magnetic dipole and expand adiabatically in velocity space. The resultant horseshoe shaped velocity distribution has been shown to be unstable with respect to a cyclotron-maser type instability (Bingham and Cairns, 2000, Vorgul et al., 2004 and Speirs et al., 2004). This instability has been postulated as the mechanism responsible for auroral kilometric radiation and also non-thermal radiation from other astrophysical bodies (Bingham et al., 2001). In this paper we describe a laboratory experiment to investigate the propagation of an electron beam subject to a magnetic compression of up to a factor of 35.

articleTitle: Time-resolved THz spectroscopy: charge carrier dynamics and the role of strongly coupled optical phonons in ultrathin graphite sheets
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Ultrafast charge carrier dynamics in graphite are investigated by time-resolved THz spectroscopy. Our data show that: (i) more than 90% of the initially deposited excitation energy is transferred to few strongly coupled lattice vibrations within 500 fs; and (ii) these optical phonons substantially contribute to the striking increase of the Drude relaxation rate.

articleTitle: Terahertz radiation from optical rectification of a modulated laser pulse
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A terahertz source has been developed based on a hybrid of optical rectification and difference frequency generation. The optical pulse from a titanium:sapphire laser system is stretched and modulated using a spatial filtering technique to produce a several picosecond long pulse modulated at the terahertz frequency. A type II phase matched interaction is realized via angle tuning in a gallium selenide crystal. A liquid helium cooled silicon bolometer was used to establish a lower bound of 2 kW on the peak power observed at 1.1 THz. Tunability was demonstrated between 0.7 and 2.0 THz.

articleTitle: Effect of resonance overlap on radiation in relativistic gyrodevices
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: The effect of overlapping resonances at different cyclotron harmonics on radiation in relativistic gyro-TWTs and gyrotwystrons is investigated through the use of self-consistent equations.

articleTitle: Development of a Ka-band second harmonic gyroklystron amplifier
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: A Ka-band second harmonic gyroklystron amplifier is developing at the Institute of Electronics, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Based on the self-consistent nonlinear calculation code GKLSC and the 2.5D particle-in-cell code CHIPIC, a conceptual design has been completed. The results show that this Ka-band three cavity gyroklystron can obtain more than 250kW output power, 28% electron efficiency, more than 26dB gain, and 110MHz bandwith. The gyroklystron prototype has been fabricated, and is preparing to do hot test.

articleTitle: An adaptive spectroellipsometric technology for the precise real-time measurements of the quality of natural and waste waters
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: Spectroellipsometry is a peak of polarization optics. The creation of multichannel polarization optical instrumentation and use of spectroellipsometric technology are very important for the real-time ecological control of aquatic environment. Spectroellipsometric devices give us high precision of measurements. Spectroellipsometric multichannel measurements in an aquatic environment provide an information basis for the application of modern algorithms for the recognition and identification of pollutants. New original elements (coaxial polarization switchers and achromatic compensators), developed in IRE RAS, allow to design cheap polarization systems (for example, spectroscopic ellipsometers, polarization spectrometers, polarimeters, dichrometers, polarization microscopes and interferometers, sensitive photometers, differential reflectometers) without expensive standard polarization elements. Principal possibility exists of use of optical and infrared bands with wavelength up to 20 Me for studies of properties of superthin coatings, films and different structures at it's base.

articleTitle: The effects of the static and dynamic screening depending on the excitation aperture size and excitation level in photoconductive THz sources
publicationTitle: 2005 Joint 30th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 13th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics
abstract: We investigate the effects of static screening caused by the generation of electron hole-pairs and the dynamic screening due to the back action of the THz radiation by the transient photocurrent as a function of excitation aperture size and excitation level in the generation of THz radiation from photoconductor.

abstract: The following topics are dealt with: THz technology, ultrafast THz measurement and imaging; THz spectroscopy and material properties; plasma and industrial applications of THz measurement; nano and quantum devices and photonic crystals; semiconductor detectors and receivers; superconductor detectors and receivers; and millimeter wave systems.
